short: The decisive engagement of the Diadochi wars that finalized the fracturing of Alexander's empire.
full:
In 301 BCE, the largest battle of the Wars of the Diadochi took place at Ipsus in Phrygia. The elderly general Antigonus I Monophthalmus, who had come closest to reuniting Alexander the Great's entire empire, faced a coalition of other successors, including Seleucus I and Cassander. The battlefield saw a massive deployment of war elephants, brought from India by Seleucus, which proved crucial in disrupting Antigonus's cavalry and isolating his son Demetrius.

Antigonus was killed in the fighting, and his ambitious project of a unified empire died with him. The victory of the coalition permanently finalized the division of the Hellenistic world into separate, rival kingdoms, setting the geopolitical boundaries that would define the eastern Mediterranean for the next two centuries.
